validity.researcher_notes: Pipeline was last updated 2023-08-07 and is now 3+ years stale. No independent documentation found: EIA carries no row for THIS proposed 2028 line in any of its 28 tracked releases (2018-05 through 2026-08) - note that EIA does carry 'Freeport LNG Pipeline', but that is the 2008 in-service feed-gas line, adjudicated below; no FERC CP docket or application found; not mentioned in Freeport LNG Development LP project announcements or SEC filings reviewed; 7 wiki citations harvested but do not directly reference this specific terminal pipeline project (references link to Freeport LNG terminal expansions completed in 2008, other LNG feed lines like TTC Connector to Coastal Bend Header, and Freeport company pages). The EIA candidate match is 'Freeport LNG Pipeline (Expansion), Completed 2008, 9.8 mi, 42 in, 1750 MMcf/d, CP03-75' — a different historical project, not this proposed 2028 line. P3666 exhibits characteristics of either a stale proposal never formalized into a FERC application, or a data entry that conflates multiple Freeport projects (the existing 2008 expansion vs. a proposed new feed). Candidate: Freeport LNG Terminal Pipeline may be a provisional/conceptual project not advanced to regulatory filing stage. | ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-14, sweep 7(a) review: the EIA-silence statement above was re-tested mechanically against sources/eia_pipeline_projects/data/eia_projects_long.csv. None is this row's 10.60 mi / 740 MMcf/d / 2028 proposal. The leading clause was reworded so a reviewer is not left with a flat absence claim, and the release range was corrected (EIA's tracked series begins 2018-05, not Feb 2018). The existence concern is unchanged and still owed FERC eLibrary and a Freeport LNG Train 4 filing search.
